chapters.title: Survivors ask for guidance
chapters.summary: The officers and all the people come to Jeremiah. They ask him to pray that the LORD will show them the way. They promise to obey, whether the answer is pleasant or not. After ten days the word comes. If they stay in the land, God will build them up and plant them. They need not fear the king of Babylon. If they go to Egypt, the sword and famine will follow them there. Jeremiah says they deceived themselves when they asked.
chapters.meaning: Verse 6 is a promise made before the answer is known. The people will obey “whether it is good, or whether it is bad.” They had already camped on the road to Egypt (41:17). Verse 7 makes them wait ten days. The answer goes against the plan they had formed. Verse 10 offers the building and planting of 1:10. Verse 20 says they misled themselves when they asked.

lds.text: What part of the survivors’ promise becomes difficult when Jeremiah gives the answer?

chapters.historicalNote: Their promise includes answers they may dislike. The warning challenges their belief that moving to Egypt would remove war and hunger.

chapters.title: The survivors reject the answer
chapters.summary: The officers tell Jeremiah he is lying. They say Baruch has turned him against them. They lead all the people into Egypt, with Jeremiah and Baruch. They settle at Tahpanhes. There the LORD tells Jeremiah to bury large stones at the entrance to Pharaoh’s house. Nebuchadnezzar will set his throne over those stones. He will strike Egypt and burn the houses of its gods.
chapters.meaning: The people promised to obey any answer (42:6). In verse 2 they call the answer a lie. Verse 3 gives their way out. They do not address the warning itself. They accuse the scribe Baruch of hidden motives. Blaming a third person lets them reject the message. Jeremiah is taken to the very place he warned against, and he keeps speaking there.

lds.text: How does blaming Baruch help the leaders reject Jeremiah’s message?

chapters.historicalNote: Their accusations avoid answering God’s warning. The buried stones show Babylon reaching the place they believe is safe.

chapters.title: A dispute about the queen of the sky
chapters.summary: The LORD’s word comes to the Jews living across Egypt. They have seen Jerusalem ruined because of offerings to other gods. Jeremiah asks why they repeat that sin in Egypt. The men and women answer that they will not listen. They will keep burning incense to the queen of the sky. When they did so in Judah, they had food and safety. Since they stopped, they have lacked everything. Jeremiah answers that the LORD remembered those offerings, and events will show whose word stands.
chapters.meaning: Both sides argue from the same events. The people say trouble began when they stopped their offerings (verse 18). Jeremiah says trouble came because they made them (verses 21–23). Each reads the past as proof. Verse 17 shows the people appealing to their fathers and kings. The dispute is about the remembered cause of a disaster. Verse 28 leaves the test to the outcome.

lds.text: How do the women and Jeremiah explain the lost food and peace differently?

chapters.historicalNote: The speakers give opposite causes for the same disaster. Data Over Dogma favors identifying the queen with Astarte. The passage does not name her.

chapters.title: Baruch receives a promise of survival
chapters.summary: This short word is for Baruch, Jeremiah’s scribe. It dates from the year he wrote the scroll. Baruch has said that the LORD added sorrow to his pain. He is worn out and finds no rest. The LORD says he is tearing down what he built across the whole land. He asks whether Baruch seeks great things for himself. Baruch should not seek them. He will keep his life wherever he goes.
chapters.meaning: Baruch came from a family of officials; his brother served the king (51:59). He could have hoped for a career. Verse 4 puts God’s own loss first. God is breaking down what he himself built and planted. Against that, verse 5 asks about Baruch’s private hopes. Personal ambition is out of scale in such a time. He is promised one thing: his life.

lds.text: What does Baruch receive instead of the greatness he seeks?

chapters.historicalNote: The promise offers survival during widespread loss rather than personal fame. It answers Baruch’s hopes without denying his sorrow.

chapters.title: Egypt’s armies face defeat
chapters.summary: This is the first of Jeremiah’s messages about foreign nations. Egypt’s army is defeated at Carchemish by the king of Babylon. Its soldiers are terrified and fall back. Egypt rose like the Nile and said it would cover the earth. No medicine will heal it. A second message says Nebuchadnezzar will invade Egypt itself. Pharaoh is called a loud noise who missed his moment. Afterward Egypt will be lived in again, and Jacob need not fear.
chapters.meaning: The Nile’s yearly flood was Egypt’s strength and pride. Verse 8 uses it as a picture of the army. Egypt says it will rise and cover the earth. Verses 5–6 have already shown the soldiers running. The boast and the outcome stand side by side. Verse 17 gives Pharaoh a mocking nickname. Verse 26 still says Egypt will be inhabited again.

lds.text: How does Egypt’s boast differ from the soldiers’ flight?

chapters.historicalNote: Egypt’s boast of covering the land fails before the attack. Its many soldiers and hired fighters cannot stop its defeat.

chapters.title: A warning against the Philistines
chapters.summary: This message concerns the Philistines. Waters rise from the north and become an overflowing flood. People cry out at the sound of horses and chariots. Fathers are too weak to turn back for their children. Tyre and Sidon lose their last helpers. Gaza and Ashkelon are silenced. A voice asks how long the LORD’s sword will keep striking. The answer is that the LORD has given it an order.
chapters.meaning: Verse 6 speaks to the sword itself. A voice asks how long before it will be quiet. It begs the sword to go back into its sheath. Verse 7 answers that it cannot rest while it has orders. The message is against an old enemy of Israel. It still contains a cry for the killing to stop. Verse 3 shows the cost: fathers who cannot help their children.

lds.text: Why does the passage ask the sword to rest?

chapters.historicalNote: The request for a quiet sword gives suffering a voice. The answer presents continued war as part of the announced judgment.

chapters.title: Moab’s pride and suffering
chapters.summary: This long message concerns Moab. Its towns are named one by one as they fall. Its god Chemosh goes into exile with his priests. Moab has been at ease since its youth, like wine left undisturbed. It mocked Israel and was very proud. The speaker wails for Moab and weeps for its vineyards. Joy and gladness are gone from its fields. Yet the LORD will restore Moab’s fortunes in the last days.
chapters.meaning: Verse 29 states the charge against Moab: great pride. Verse 27 adds that it laughed at Israel. Then verse 31 says, “I will wail for Moab.” The voice that judges also mourns. Verse 36 says the speaker’s heart moans like a flute. Judgment and grief come from the same mouth. Verse 47 ends the chapter with a promise of restoration.

lds.text: How does the mourning for Moab complicate the warning against its pride?

chapters.historicalNote: Moab’s wealth and ease cannot prevent loss. Grief for the victims remains beside the charge of pride.

chapters.title: Warnings against neighboring peoples
chapters.summary: This chapter gathers messages about five peoples. Ammon trusted in its treasures and will see its capital ruined. Edom trusted in its wisdom and its high cliffs. Damascus grows weak, and its young men fall in the streets. The desert tribes of Kedar lose their tents and camels. Elam’s bow is broken, and its people are scattered. Ammon and Elam are promised restoration afterward. God says he will keep Edom’s orphans alive.
chapters.meaning: Each people in this chapter relied on something different. Ammon had treasure and fertile valleys (verse 4). Edom had wisdom and cliffs (verses 7 and 16). Damascus had fame, Kedar had distance, and Elam had the bow. Every one of these protections fails. The endings are not the same. Ammon and Elam are restored, and Edom’s orphans are kept (verses 6, 11, 39).

lds.text: Which kinds of protection fail in these warnings?

chapters.historicalNote: Treasures, mountain defenses, and weapons fail to provide lasting safety. God promises return to Ammon and Elam. The other warnings offer no matching promise.

chapters.title: Babylon faces judgment
chapters.summary: This message announces the fall of Babylon. Its gods are put to shame, and a nation from the north attacks. Israel and Judah come weeping and ask the way to Zion. They have been lost sheep, misled by their shepherds. Their enemies said harming them was no crime, since they had sinned. Assyria devoured Israel, and Babylon gnawed its bones. God will punish Babylon as he punished Assyria. The hammer of the whole earth is broken.
chapters.meaning: Verse 7 quotes the enemies’ defense. Israel sinned against the LORD, so those who devoured it are “not guilty.” They borrow the prophets’ own teaching to excuse themselves. The chapter rejects that excuse. Verse 11 says Babylon rejoiced as it plundered. Verse 29 says it was proud against the LORD. Being the means of judgment did not make its cruelty innocent.

lds.text: Why does Babylon remain responsible after serving as an instrument of judgment?

chapters.historicalNote: Babylon’s earlier role in punishment does not excuse its violence. The warning holds the conqueror responsible for harming the people it captured.

chapters.title: A scroll marks Babylon’s announced fall
chapters.summary: The LORD will send a destroying wind against Babylon. Babylon was a golden cup that made the whole earth drunk. Now it falls suddenly, and its wound cannot be healed. The LORD made the earth by his power, and idols are nothing. Zion says Nebuchadnezzar swallowed her like a monster. Babylon’s thick walls will be leveled. Jeremiah writes all this in a scroll and gives it to an officer named Seraiah. Seraiah must read it in Babylon and sink it in the Euphrates.
chapters.meaning: Verse 59 dates this to Zedekiah’s fourth year. In that same period Jeremiah told the exiles to pray for Babylon (29:7). The exiles should seek the city’s peace, and its fall is already written. Jeremiah wrote this in a book (verse 60); the palette shows a scribe’s tools. Seraiah is to read the scroll aloud in Babylon. A stone then sends the scroll beneath the river’s surface. Verse 64 explains the act: Babylon will sink and not rise.

lds.text: Why does Jeremiah tell Seraiah to sink the scroll after reading it?

chapters.historicalNote: The sinking scroll gives visible form to Babylon’s announced fall. People must leave Babylon to avoid sharing its punishment.

chapters.title: Jerusalem’s destruction and Jehoiachin’s release
chapters.summary: This last chapter retells the fall of Jerusalem. Zedekiah rebels, and Babylon besieges the city until the food is gone. The wall is breached, and the king is caught and blinded. The temple, the palace, and the houses are burned. The bronze pillars and vessels of the temple are carried away. The chief priests and officials are executed. The numbers of the exiles are listed. Years later the king of Babylon frees Jehoiachin and feeds him at his table.
chapters.meaning: Chapter 51:64 said Jeremiah’s words ended there. This chapter adds history that matches 2 Kings 25. It shows that the city fell as he had said. Verses 17–23 list the temple’s bronze piece by piece as it is taken. Nothing is said to repair that loss. Verse 31 then reports a small mercy to a captive king. The book ends with a ruined temple and a living heir of David.

lds.text: What changes for Jehoiachin, and what losses remain unchanged?

chapters.historicalNote: Invaders break and carry away Solomon’s temple furnishings. Jehoiachin’s changed treatment offers limited hope without reversing the destruction.

people.name: Jeremiah
people.role: Prophet who warns Judah and speaks about its return
people.relations: He is Hilkiah’s son, from the priests of Anathoth. Baruch writes his words, and Judah’s officials jail him.
people.meaning: God calls him when he says he is too young to speak. He warns the temple crowd, and Pashhur puts him in stocks. Officials throw him in a pit, and Ebedmelech pulls him out. After the city falls, survivors take him to Egypt.

people.name: Hilkiah, Jeremiah’s father
people.role: Priest named as Jeremiah’s father
people.relations: He is Jeremiah’s father and one of the priests in Anathoth.
people.meaning: The first verse names him as Jeremiah’s father. He is one of the priests in Anathoth in Benjamin. The book does not say he is the high priest of Josiah’s time.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Josiah
people.role: King during the start of Jeremiah’s work
people.relations: He is Amon’s son. Jehoiakim, Shallum, and Zedekiah are his sons.
people.meaning: God’s word first comes to Jeremiah in his thirteenth year as king. Later Jeremiah reminds Jehoiakim of him. Josiah did what was fair and judged the cause of the poor. Jeremiah says it went well with him then.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Amon, king of Judah
people.role: Josiah’s father, named in two dates
people.relations: He is Josiah’s father.
people.meaning: The book names him only as Josiah’s father. His name appears where the book dates Jeremiah’s first message. He does nothing in this book.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jehoiakim
people.role: King who uses unpaid labor and burns Jeremiah’s scroll
people.relations: He is Josiah’s son and Jehoiachin’s father.
people.meaning: Jeremiah says he builds his house with workers he does not pay. He has the prophet Uriah brought back from Egypt and kills him. Jehudi reads him Jeremiah’s scroll. He cuts it up and burns it, though three officials beg him not to.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Zedekiah, king of Judah
people.role: King who asks Jeremiah in secret but will not surrender
people.relations: He is Josiah’s son, and Hamutal is his mother. Nebuchadnezzar makes him king, then captures and blinds him.
people.meaning: He sends men to ask Jeremiah for help against Babylon. He lets the officials put Jeremiah in a pit, then lets Ebedmelech save him. Jeremiah tells him to give himself up, but he fears being mocked. He runs at night and is caught near Jericho.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Nebuchadnezzar
people.role: Babylonian king whose armies capture Jerusalem
people.relations: He makes Zedekiah king and later judges him at Riblah. He tells Nebuzaradan to take care of Jeremiah.
people.meaning: God calls him “my servant” and gives the nations into his hand. His army surrounds Jerusalem and breaks in. At Riblah he kills Zedekiah’s sons and puts out Zedekiah’s eyes. The book also says Babylon will be punished in its turn.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jehoiachin / Jeconiah / Coniah
people.role: Judean king taken to Babylon and later released from prison
people.relations: He is Jehoiakim’s son. His mother and the princes of Judah go to Babylon with him.
people.meaning: The book also calls him Jeconiah and Coniah. Jeremiah says God will cast him and his mother into another land. Nebuchadnezzar carries him to Babylon. In the thirty-seventh year, Evilmerodach frees him from prison and feeds him each day.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Shallum / Jehoahaz, king of Judah
people.role: Josiah’s son who is led away and will not return
people.relations: He is Josiah’s son and became king after him.
people.meaning: Jeremiah calls him Shallum. He became king after Josiah and then was led away captive. Jeremiah tells the people to weep for him, not for the dead. He will die where he was taken and not see his land again.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: David
people.role: Earlier king whose family is promised a fair ruler
people.relations: Jeremiah calls Judah’s royal family the house of David.
people.meaning: Jeremiah tells the house of David to do justice every morning. God promises to raise a righteous Branch for David. That king will rule fairly, and Judah will be safe. God says David will never lack a man on the throne.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Manasseh, king of Judah
people.role: Earlier king whose acts God blames
people.relations: He is Hezekiah’s son and a king of Judah.
people.meaning: God says he will toss Judah among all the kingdoms. He gives the reason: what Manasseh did in Jerusalem. The verse does not list those acts.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Moses
people.role: Earlier leader God names with Samuel
people.relations: God names him beside Samuel.
people.meaning: God says he would not turn toward Judah even if Moses stood before him. Moses does nothing else in this book. God names him to show that no one’s plea will help now.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Samuel
people.role: Earlier prophet named beside Moses
people.relations: God names him beside Moses.
people.meaning: God says he would not turn toward Judah even if Samuel stood before him. Samuel does nothing else in this book. His name shows that pleading for Judah will not work now.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Rachel
people.role: Mother heard weeping for her children in Ramah
people.relations: The poem calls the lost people her children.
people.meaning: A voice is heard in Ramah. Rachel weeps for her children and will not be comforted, because they are gone. God tells her to stop weeping. He says her children will come back from the enemy’s land.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Baruch
people.role: Writer who records and reads Jeremiah’s words
people.relations: He is Neriah’s son. He writes for Jeremiah, and Johanan’s group takes both men to Egypt.
people.meaning: He stores the deeds for Jeremiah’s field in a clay jar. He writes Jeremiah’s words on a scroll and reads it at the temple. After the king burns it, he writes it again. When he complains of sorrow, God promises him his life.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Pashhur, son of Immer
people.role: Temple officer who strikes Jeremiah and puts him in stocks
people.relations: He is the son of Immer the priest. He is not Pashhur the son of Malchijah.
people.meaning: He hears Jeremiah’s warning and strikes him. He locks him in the stocks at the upper gate of Benjamin. The next day he lets him go. Jeremiah gives him a new name, Magormissabib, and says he will die in Babylon.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Pashhur, son of Malchijah
people.role: Official sent to Jeremiah who later asks for his death
people.relations: He is Malchijah’s son. He is not Pashhur the son of Immer.
people.meaning: Zedekiah sends him with Zephaniah to ask Jeremiah for God’s help against Babylon. Later he hears Jeremiah tell the people to go out to the Chaldeans. He and three other officials ask the king to put Jeremiah to death.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Zephaniah, the priest
people.role: Priest who carries the king’s requests to Jeremiah
people.relations: He is Maaseiah’s son and the second priest. The king of Babylon kills him at Riblah.
people.meaning: Zedekiah sends him to Jeremiah twice, once to ask for help and once for prayer. Shemaiah writes to him and asks why he has not punished Jeremiah. Zephaniah reads that letter to Jeremiah. After the city falls, Nebuzaradan takes him to Riblah.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Hananiah, son of Azzur
people.role: Prophet who says Babylon’s rule will end in two years
people.relations: He is Azzur’s son, from Gibeon. He speaks against Jeremiah in the temple.
people.meaning: He says God will bring back the temple vessels and the captives within two years. He takes the wooden bar off Jeremiah’s neck and breaks it. Jeremiah tells him God did not send him and he will die that year. He dies in the seventh month.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Uriah, son of Shemaiah
people.role: Prophet killed for warnings like Jeremiah’s
people.relations: He is Shemaiah’s son, from Kiriath Jearim. Jehoiakim sends Elnathan to bring him back from Egypt.
people.meaning: He speaks against the city and the land, as Jeremiah does. Jehoiakim wants him dead, so he flees to Egypt. The king’s men bring him back. Jehoiakim kills him with the sword and throws his body among the common graves.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Micah, the Morashtite
people.role: Earlier prophet whose warning helps defend Jeremiah
people.relations: He spoke in the days of Hezekiah, king of Judah.
people.meaning: Some elders quote him at Jeremiah’s hearing. Micah said Zion would be plowed like a field. Hezekiah did not kill him for it. The elders use this to argue that Jeremiah should live.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Hezekiah
people.role: Earlier king recalled for hearing Micah’s warning
people.relations: Micah spoke in his days. Manasseh is named as his son.
people.meaning: The elders recall how he heard Micah’s warning. He did not put Micah to death. He feared the LORD and asked for his favor, and the disaster did not come. The elders set this beside the call to kill Jeremiah.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Ahikam
people.role: Official who keeps Jeremiah from being killed
people.relations: He is Shaphan’s son and Gedaliah’s father.
people.meaning: The crowd at the temple wants Jeremiah dead. Ahikam stands with Jeremiah, so he is not handed over to the people. Later the book names him as the father of Gedaliah.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Shaphan
people.role: Father of several officials who help Jeremiah
people.relations: Ahikam, Elasah, and Gemariah are named as his sons. Gedaliah and Micaiah are his grandsons.
people.meaning: Shaphan does nothing himself in this book. His son Ahikam protects Jeremiah. His son Elasah carries Jeremiah’s letter to Babylon. Baruch reads the scroll in the room of his son Gemariah.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Elnathan, son of Achbor
people.role: Official who brings Uriah back and later defends the scroll
people.relations: He is Achbor’s son. He serves King Jehoiakim.
people.meaning: Jehoiakim sends him to Egypt with men to bring back Uriah. Uriah is then killed. Later he hears Baruch read the scroll. He begs the king not to burn it, but the king does not listen.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Elasah, son of Shaphan
people.role: Messenger who carries Jeremiah’s letter to Babylon
people.relations: He is Shaphan’s son. He travels with Gemariah the son of Hilkiah.
people.meaning: Zedekiah sends him to Nebuchadnezzar in Babylon. He carries Jeremiah’s letter to the captives there. The letter tells them to build houses and plant gardens. He appears only in this verse.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Gemariah, son of Hilkiah
people.role: Messenger who helps carry Jeremiah’s letter to Babylon
people.relations: He is Hilkiah’s son. He is not Gemariah the son of Shaphan.
people.meaning: Zedekiah sends him to Babylon with Elasah. The two carry Jeremiah’s letter to the captives. The text does not say which Hilkiah is his father.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Ahab, son of Kolaiah
people.role: Prophet in Babylon whom Jeremiah says lies
people.relations: He is Kolaiah’s son. Jeremiah names him beside Zedekiah the son of Maaseiah.
people.meaning: Jeremiah’s letter says he tells lies in God’s name. It also charges him with adultery with his neighbors’ wives. God will hand him to Nebuchadnezzar, who will kill him in front of the captives. The captives will use his name in a curse.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Zedekiah, son of Maaseiah
people.role: Prophet in Babylon whom Jeremiah says lies
people.relations: He is Maaseiah’s son. He is not King Zedekiah.
people.meaning: Jeremiah’s letter names him with Ahab as a lying prophet in Babylon. It charges both with adultery with their neighbors’ wives. God will hand them to Nebuchadnezzar to be killed. A curse will recall that the king roasted them in the fire.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Shemaiah, the Nehelamite
people.role: Man in Babylon who writes to have Jeremiah punished
people.relations: He writes to Zephaniah the priest and to the people in Jerusalem.
people.meaning: He hears Jeremiah’s message that the captivity will be long. He writes to Zephaniah and asks why Jeremiah is not in the stocks. Jeremiah answers that God did not send Shemaiah. None of his family will see the good God will do.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Hanamel
people.role: Jeremiah’s cousin who offers him a field in Anathoth
people.relations: He is the son of Shallum, Jeremiah’s uncle.
people.meaning: He comes to Jeremiah in the court of the guard. He asks Jeremiah to buy his field in Anathoth. Jeremiah pays seventeen shekels of silver and signs the deed. God says houses and fields will be bought in this land again.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: The Rechabites
people.role: Family who will not drink wine
people.relations: They call Jonadab the son of Rechab their father. Jaazaniah is named with them.
people.meaning: Jeremiah brings them to a temple room and sets wine before them. They refuse, because Jonadab told them never to drink wine. They also live in tents, as he said. God sets them beside Judah, who has not listened to him.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jaazaniah, the Rechabite
people.role: Rechabite whom Jeremiah brings to the temple
people.relations: He is the son of another Jeremiah, the son of Habazziniah.
people.meaning: Jeremiah takes him, his brothers, and his sons to the temple. The whole house of the Rechabites comes too. The text names him first but gives him no words of his own.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jonadab / Jehonadab
people.role: Father whose rules the Rechabites keep
people.relations: He is Rechab’s son. The Rechabites call him their father.
people.meaning: He told his family never to drink wine. He told them to build no houses and to live in tents. In Jeremiah’s day they still obey. God promises that Jonadab will always have a man to stand before him.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Gemariah, son of Shaphan
people.role: Official whose temple room Baruch reads in
people.relations: He is the son of Shaphan the scribe. Micaiah is his son.
people.meaning: Baruch reads the scroll to the people in his room at the temple. His son Micaiah tells the officials what he heard. Gemariah hears the scroll with them. He begs the king not to burn it, but the king will not listen.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Micaiah, son of Gemariah
people.role: Listener who tells the officials what Baruch read
people.relations: He is the son of Gemariah and the grandson of Shaphan.
people.meaning: He hears Baruch read the scroll at the temple. He goes down to the king’s house and tells the officials. They send for Baruch, and the scroll reaches the king.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Elishama, the scribe
people.role: Scribe whose room holds the scroll
people.relations: He sits with the officials who hear Baruch.
people.meaning: He is with the officials when Micaiah brings news of the scroll. They hear Baruch read it. They leave the scroll in his room and go to tell the king. Jehudi takes it from there to read to the king.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Delaiah, son of Shemaiah
people.role: Official who asks the king not to burn the scroll
people.relations: He is Shemaiah’s son. He joins Elnathan and Gemariah in asking the king.
people.meaning: He sits with the officials who hear Baruch read the scroll. They tell Baruch and Jeremiah to hide. He asks the king not to burn the scroll. The king does not listen.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Zedekiah, son of Hananiah
people.role: Official who sits with the princes in the scribe’s room
people.relations: He is Hananiah’s son. He is not King Zedekiah.
people.meaning: He sits with the officials when Micaiah reports Baruch’s reading. The text names him once and gives him no act of his own.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jehudi
people.role: Messenger who reads the scroll to Jehoiakim
people.relations: He is the son of Nethaniah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Cushi.
people.meaning: The officials send him to bring Baruch and the scroll. Later the king sends him to get the scroll from Elishama’s room. He reads three or four columns to the king. The king cuts the scroll and burns it all.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: The officers sent to arrest Jeremiah and Baruch
people.role: Three men the king sends to arrest Jeremiah and Baruch
people.relations: Jerahmeel is called the king’s son. Seraiah is Azriel’s son, and Shelemiah is Abdeel’s son.
people.meaning: After he burns the scroll, Jehoiakim tells these three to seize Baruch and Jeremiah. They do not find them. The text says the LORD hid them.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jehucal / Jucal, son of Shelemiah
people.role: Official who asks for prayer and later for Jeremiah’s death
people.relations: He is Shelemiah’s son. Zedekiah sends him with Zephaniah the priest.
people.meaning: Zedekiah sends him to ask Jeremiah to pray for the people. Later he hears Jeremiah tell the people to go out to the Chaldeans. He joins the officials who ask the king to kill Jeremiah. The text spells his name Jehucal and Jucal.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Irijah
people.role: Guard captain who arrests Jeremiah at the gate
people.relations: He is the son of Shelemiah, the son of Hananiah.
people.meaning: He stops Jeremiah at Benjamin’s gate and says he is going over to the Chaldeans. Jeremiah says that is false. Irijah does not listen and takes him to the officials. They beat Jeremiah and put him in prison.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jonathan, the scribe
people.role: Scribe whose house becomes Jeremiah’s prison
people.relations: The text calls him the scribe. He is not Jonathan the son of Kareah.
people.meaning: The officials make his house the prison and put Jeremiah in its cells. Jeremiah stays there many days. He begs Zedekiah not to send him back, or he will die there. Jonathan himself does not act or speak.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Shephatiah and Gedaliah, the officials opposing Jeremiah
people.role: Two officials who ask the king to kill Jeremiah
people.relations: Shephatiah is Mattan’s son. Gedaliah is Pashhur’s son, and is not Gedaliah the governor.
people.meaning: They hear Jeremiah tell the people to go out to the Chaldeans and live. With Jucal and Pashhur, they tell the king he weakens the soldiers. The king gives Jeremiah into their hands. They lower him into a pit of mud.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Malchijah, the king’s son
people.role: King’s son whose pit holds Jeremiah
people.relations: He is called the king’s son. The text does not say he is Pashhur’s father.
people.meaning: The officials throw Jeremiah into his pit in the court of the guard. The pit has no water, only mud, and Jeremiah sinks in it. Malchijah himself does nothing in the story.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Ebedmelech / Ebed-melech
people.role: Ethiopian palace servant who rescues Jeremiah
people.relations: He is an Ethiopian who serves in King Zedekiah’s house.
people.meaning: He hears that Jeremiah is in the pit and warns the king he will die. The king gives him thirty men. He lowers old rags for Jeremiah to pad the ropes, then pulls him out. God promises Ebedmelech that he will live when the city falls.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: The Babylonian officers at Jerusalem
people.role: Babylonian officials who sit in the gate and free Jeremiah
people.relations: Verse 3 lists Nergal Sharezer, Samgarnebo, Sarsechim, and a second Nergal Sharezer. Verse 13 names Nebushazban and Nergal Sharezer with Nebuzaradan.
people.meaning: They enter Jerusalem when the wall is broken and sit in the middle gate. Later they send for Jeremiah and take him out of the court of the guard. They hand him to Gedaliah. The text does not say if the two Nergal Sharezer names are one man.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Nebuzaradan
people.role: Babylonian captain who burns the city and frees Jeremiah
people.relations: He is Nebuchadnezzar’s captain of the guard. He leaves the remaining people with Gedaliah.
people.meaning: He burns the temple, the king’s house, and the houses of Jerusalem. He carries people to Babylon and leaves the poorest to farm. At Ramah he takes off Jeremiah’s chains and lets him choose where to go. He takes Seraiah and Zephaniah to Riblah.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Gedaliah, son of Ahikam
people.role: Governor placed over Judah’s remaining people
people.relations: He is Ahikam’s son and Shaphan’s grandson. He is not Gedaliah the son of Pashhur.
people.meaning: The king of Babylon makes him governor, and he lives at Mizpah. He tells the commanders to serve Babylon and gather wine, fruit, and oil. Johanan warns him about Ishmael, but he does not believe it. Ishmael kills him at a meal in Mizpah.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Ishmael, son of Nethaniah
people.role: Man of the royal family who kills Gedaliah
people.relations: He is the son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama. Johanan says Baalis sent him.
people.meaning: He eats with Gedaliah at Mizpah, then kills him with ten men. Two days later he kills most of eighty men who come with offerings. He takes the people of Mizpah captive and heads for Ammon. Johanan catches him at Gibeon, and he escapes with eight men.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Johanan, son of Kareah
people.role: Commander who warns Gedaliah and later leads the people to Egypt
people.relations: He is Kareah’s son and Jonathan’s brother. He warns Gedaliah, fights Ishmael, and argues with Jeremiah.
people.meaning: He tells Gedaliah that Ishmael plans to kill him and offers to kill Ishmael first. After the murder he frees Ishmael’s captives at Gibeon. He asks Jeremiah to pray, calls the answer a lie, and leads all to Egypt.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jonathan, son of Kareah
people.role: Commander named beside his brother Johanan
people.relations: He is Kareah’s son and Johanan’s brother. He is not Jonathan the scribe.
people.meaning: He comes with his brother and the other commanders to Gedaliah at Mizpah. Gedaliah tells them to serve the king of Babylon. The text names him only here.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Seraiah, son of Tanhumeth
people.role: Commander who comes to Gedaliah at Mizpah
people.relations: He is Tanhumeth’s son. He is not Seraiah the son of Neriah or Seraiah the chief priest.
people.meaning: He comes with his men to Gedaliah at Mizpah. Gedaliah tells the commanders not to fear serving the Chaldeans. The text names him only in this list.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jezaniah / Jaazaniah, the Maacathite’s son
people.role: Commander who joins the gathering at Mizpah
people.relations: The text calls him the son of the Maacathite. It does not link him with Jezaniah the son of Hoshaiah.
people.meaning: He comes with his men to Gedaliah at Mizpah. Gedaliah tells the commanders to gather wine, summer fruits, and oil. The text names him only in this list.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Baalis
people.role: Ammonite king whom Johanan accuses of sending Ishmael
people.relations: He is king of the children of Ammon. Johanan links him with Ishmael.
people.meaning: Johanan tells Gedaliah that Baalis has sent Ishmael to kill him. Gedaliah does not believe it. The text gives only Johanan’s report. Later Ishmael does kill Gedaliah and flees toward Ammon.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jezaniah, son of Hoshaiah
people.role: Leader who asks Jeremiah to pray for the survivors
people.relations: He is Hoshaiah’s son and stands with Johanan. Azariah in 43:2 is also called Hoshaiah’s son.
people.meaning: He comes with Johanan and all the people to Jeremiah. They ask him to pray that God will show them the way. They promise to obey, whether the answer is good or bad. The text does not say if he and Azariah are one man.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Azariah, son of Hoshaiah
people.role: Leader who accuses Jeremiah of lying about Egypt
people.relations: He is Hoshaiah’s son and speaks with Johanan. Jezaniah in 42:1 is also called Hoshaiah’s son.
people.meaning: Jeremiah tells the people not to go to Egypt. Azariah tells him he speaks falsely. He says Baruch turned Jeremiah against them to hand them to the Chaldeans. The text does not say if he and Jezaniah are one man.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: The women defending offerings to the queen
people.role: Judean women in Egypt who burn incense to the queen of the sky
people.relations: They say their husbands knew of the cakes and drink offerings.
people.meaning: They and their husbands tell Jeremiah they will not listen to him. They say food was plenty when they burned incense to the queen of the sky. They say hunger and the sword came when they stopped. Jeremiah answers that the incense itself brought the disaster.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Pharaoh Hophra
people.role: Egyptian king named in Jeremiah’s warning
people.relations: Jeremiah sets him beside Zedekiah, whom Nebuchadnezzar took.
people.meaning: The people of Judah have gone to Egypt to be safe. God says he will give Hophra to enemies who seek his life. This will be the sign that God’s words against them stand.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Pharaoh Necoh / Neco
people.role: Egyptian king whose army is struck at Carchemish
people.relations: His army faces Nebuchadnezzar by the river Euphrates.
people.meaning: The message about Egypt opens with his army at Carchemish. Nebuchadnezzar strikes it in the fourth year of Jehoiakim. The verse says no more about Necoh himself.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Seraiah, son of Neriah
people.role: Official told to read Jeremiah’s Babylon scroll and sink it
people.relations: He is the son of Neriah, the son of Mahseiah. Baruch is called by the same father and grandfather.
people.meaning: He goes with King Zedekiah to Babylon in the king’s fourth year. Jeremiah gives him a scroll of all the evil coming on Babylon. He must read it there and tie a stone to it. Then he must throw it in the Euphrates. He must say that Babylon will sink the same way.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Hamutal
people.role: Zedekiah’s mother, named in the last chapter
people.relations: She is Zedekiah’s mother and the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
people.meaning: The last chapter names her when it tells of Zedekiah’s reign. Her father is Jeremiah of Libnah. The prophet Jeremiah is from Anathoth, not Libnah. She does nothing in the story.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Seraiah, the chief priest
people.role: Chief priest taken and killed after Jerusalem falls
people.relations: Nebuzaradan takes him with Zephaniah the second priest. He is not Seraiah the son of Neriah.
people.meaning: Nebuzaradan takes him from the city with Zephaniah and three keepers of the threshold. He brings them to the king of Babylon at Riblah. The king puts them to death there.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Solomon
people.role: Earlier king who made the temple’s bronze pieces
people.relations: The text says King Solomon made them for the LORD’s house.
people.meaning: The Chaldeans break up the bronze pillars, the sea, and the twelve bronze bulls. They carry the bronze to Babylon. The text says King Solomon had made these things. He does nothing else in this book.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Evilmerodach / Evil Merodach
people.role: Babylonian king who releases Jehoiachin from prison
people.relations: He is king of Babylon and deals kindly with Jehoiachin.
people.meaning: In his first year he lets Jehoiachin out of prison. He speaks kindly to him and gives him a seat above the other captive kings. He changes his prison clothes. He gives him food every day for the rest of his life.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Jeremiah warns the city in the temple, at the gates, and in the king’s house. In chapter 39 Babylon’s army breaks in. In chapter 52 Nebuzaradan burns the temple and the houses.
places.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.

places.name: Anathoth · proposed locality
places.summary: Jeremiah comes from the priests of Anathoth (chapter 1). Men of Anathoth threaten his life in chapter 11. In chapter 32 he buys Hanamel’s field there.
places.limits: More than one site has been proposed for Anathoth. The marker shows one general location.

places.name: Babylon
places.summary: Nebuchadnezzar carries Jeconiah and many others here (chapter 24). Jeremiah sends the captives a letter in chapter 29. Chapters 50 and 51 say Babylon itself will fall.
places.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.

places.name: Mizpah · Benjamin identification uncertain
places.summary: Gedaliah governs from Mizpah, and Jeremiah lives with him there (chapter 40). In chapter 41 Ishmael kills Gedaliah and takes the people away.
places.limits: More than one site has been proposed for Mizpah. The marker shows one general location.

places.name: Ramah · Benjamin locality
places.summary: In chapter 31 a voice in Ramah is Rachel weeping for her children. In chapter 40 Nebuzaradan frees Jeremiah from his chains at Ramah.
places.limits: More than one site has been proposed for Ramah. The marker shows one general location.

places.name: Riblah · proposed Orontes locality
places.summary: Nebuchadnezzar judges Zedekiah here in chapters 39 and 52. He kills Zedekiah’s sons and puts out Zedekiah’s eyes. He also kills the chief priest Seraiah and other captives.
places.limits: The text places Riblah in the land of Hamath. The marker shows a proposed location.

places.name: Jericho
places.summary: The Chaldean army catches Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho. Chapters 39 and 52 both tell it.
places.limits: The text names the plains of Jericho, not one spot. The marker shows the town.

places.name: Carchemish
places.summary: Pharaoh Necoh’s army stands at Carchemish by the river Euphrates. Nebuchadnezzar strikes it there (chapter 46).
places.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.

places.name: Shiloh
places.summary: In chapters 7 and 26 God points the temple crowd to Shiloh. His place once stood there, and he says to see what he did to it. He says the temple in Jerusalem will become like it.
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.

places.name: Samaria
places.summary: In chapter 23 God says Samaria’s prophets spoke by Baal. He then charges Jerusalem’s prophets with adultery and lies.
places.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.

places.name: Lachish
places.summary: In chapter 34 Babylon’s army fights against Lachish. Only Lachish and Azekah are left of Judah’s walled cities.
places.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.

places.name: Azekah · traditional locality
places.summary: In chapter 34 Babylon’s army fights against Azekah. Only Azekah and Lachish are left of Judah’s walled cities.
places.limits: The marker shows the traditional location.

places.name: Gibeon · el-Jib locality
places.summary: Johanan finds Ishmael by the great waters in Gibeon (chapter 41). The captives turn back to Johanan, and Ishmael escapes with eight men.
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.

places.name: Bethlehem / Ephrath

steps.title: A temple can become a false source of safety
steps.text: Verse 4 quotes a phrase the people repeat three times. They treat the building as a guarantee. Verse 9 lists what they do during the week. It names theft, murder, adultery, false oaths, and other gods. Verse 11 calls the temple a robbers’ den, a hideout where thieves feel safe. Verse 12 points to Shiloh, an earlier holy place that fell (1 Samuel 4). Jesus quotes verse 11 in Matthew 21:13.

steps.title: A land purchase gives hope a material form
steps.text: The field lies in territory the enemy already controls. On any market it is worthless. Jeremiah still follows every legal step (verses 10–12). Verse 14 orders the deeds kept in a jar “that they may last many days.” The wait will be long. The purchase puts money behind the promise in verse 15. The tablet offers an earlier regional comparison for recording land sales.

steps.title: Destroying a copy does not end the message
steps.text: The scroll moves through writing, public reading, court officials, and the king. Baruch writes it with ink (verse 18); a scribe’s palette held such ink. The officials tremble when they hear it (verse 16). The king cuts and burns it column by column (verse 23). Verse 24 notes that he did not tear his clothes. His father Josiah did tear his at a reading (2 Kings 22:11). Verse 32 says the second scroll was longer than the first.
